scope: Live draft, accepted source/action state, PR389-400, issue386/357, existing checkpoint and LVP owner gates. Read-only; no acceptance authority.

findings.title: Current action review is pending on oversized #357 evidence
findings.location: L21: “the evidence-selection overflow is resolved for the current cycle”; L139: “Action review pending. No new action or disposition has been admitted.”
findings.explanation: The October 20 action snapshot records a 128 KiB per-source rejection for required #357 evidence, with pending review and no admitted action or decision. #391 fixed an earlier bounded local replay, not all future mandatory discussions.
findings.correction: State the observed October 20 pending result, preserve zero admissions, and separate known byte-guard behavior from unqualified token-window fit.

findings.title: Accepted October 19 closing and October 15 dispositions are misrepresented
findings.location: L101: “Three open items carry forward with explicit priority ordering from the accepted October 19 closing continuity.”; L107: “three reviewed canonical actions pending receipt.”
findings.explanation: The accepted closing contains three existing checkpoint identities for timing, recovery, and popover review. The three October 15 action IDs have deferred, completed-existing-evidence, and pending-receipt dispositions respectively; they were not the closing's ranked three and are not all pending receipt.
findings.correction: Restore checkpoint:d8e801b487140ebe8fd3, checkpoint:a2c05cce92f08451469c, and checkpoint:edd972afb47f74ef416a with their gates; if discussing October 15 records, retain each original ID and distinct disposition.

findings.title: #385 popover pilot is conflated with the scheduling candidate
findings.location: L105: “A current-base candidate exists (`5v897125`, recorded base `730fb9f`)”; L111: “Blocked on rebase before visual verdict.”
findings.explanation: 5v897125 is invalid and the valid 5f897125 is the separate Chicago scheduling candidate based on 730fb9f. #385 is the popover PR at cc3c99bc; its exact-head preview is checked and awaiting human visual review. A rebase is not established as the prerequisite for asking for that verdict.
findings.correction: Separate the 5f897125 scheduling checkpoint from #385; request a source-bound human preview verdict, then handle current-base integration and merge as separate gates.

findings.title: PR work is assigned to invented ordered pipeline stages
findings.location: L17: “action-evidence selection fixes (#390, #391)”; L19: “#393 fixed stage three (editorial receipt binding).”
findings.explanation: PR #390 registers an independent article review, #393 repairs an editorial receipt reader, and #395/#397/#400 register distinct source-current reviews. These are separate editorial, action, presentation, and delivery operations rather than sequential stages of one generation pipeline.
findings.correction: Replace the five-stage chronology with a factual account of each PR's purpose and its place in the October 19 article follow-through.

findings.title: #391 mechanism and cap rationale are invented
findings.location: L55: “scores candidate records by direct dependency ... then by recency”; “identity caps ... are empirically derived from the 640 KiB total ceiling.”
findings.explanation: Accepted source selects whole mandatory dependencies before optional sources with stable ID ordering, not dependency-recency scores. The 3-5 initial target and at-most-two new later identities came from operator policy clarification, not an empirical derivation from the 640 KiB byte ceiling.
findings.correction: Describe required-source classification, whole-source inclusion and recorded omissions; attribute identity bounds to policy and distinguish them from byte guards.

findings.title: #393 historical provenance claim exceeds observed repair
findings.location: L69: “The chain for earlier receipts is best-effort.”; L67: “check whether the PR head SHA in the receipt matches the current PR head SHA”.
findings.explanation: The exact #392 captured receipt kept immutable input and artifact heads while an embedded PR object advanced after the push. The repaired reader accepted that unedited old receipt with immutable checks intact. A current PR-head mismatch alone does not make all pre-#393 receipts best-effort.
findings.correction: Limit the diagnosis to the mutable embedded PR object and actual #392 replay; remove the blanket historical-receipt downgrade.

findings.title: Legacy heading and fixture changes are misstated
findings.location: L95: “Without fixture isolation, tests ... would suppress failures in the new three-option path”; “normalization was applied retroactively to in-flight history.”
findings.explanation: bf67063 changed heading extraction and tests without rewriting historical article data. fe84ab6 froze authentic old two-option data for historical tests and added current three-item assertions after six tests failed against mutable current data; there is no evidence that old fixtures had masked present regressions.
findings.correction: Describe the parser coverage and static historical fixture repair accurately; remove retroactive-history and predicted adjacent-suite claims.

findings.title: LEGO design PR exits and owners are collapsed
findings.location: L113: “No active development work is gated on them”; L155: “No owner action is required in the current cycle.”
findings.explanation: LVP #44 and #46 are non-operative overlays with close-or-supersede/import conditions, while #45 has a separate HOUSE-WORLD record, second-steward check, and James's merge control. #46 also assigns future Grid/Subgrid, navigation, and motion work. Blanket no-owner-action language is false.
findings.correction: Preserve the three records' distinct exits and owner gates; mark any parking review as an editorial proposal subject to those owners.

findings.title: Shipment and issue links are malformed
findings.location: L15: `#https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/389` links to `/pull/https://.../389`; L21/L121/L123 route issues #386/#357 to `/pull/`.
findings.explanation: All 11 heading links contain duplicated GitHub URL segments. #386 and #357 are issue records but link to pull-request paths. The live dated API has all 11 correct mergerows and one phantom unavailable pull/386 row; this is a reference-classification defect, not absent merge-time coverage.
findings.correction: Render short #389-#400 PR labels with direct /pull/N links; route #386 and #357 to /issues/N and remove the phantom unavailable pull/386 shipment-time reference while retaining all 11 real merge controls.

findings.title: Live API's 32 commit references are not the 25 distinct shipments
findings.location: L3 title: “25 commits”; L23–47 list 25 SHA entries; live API field `commitCount: 32`.
findings.explanation: The article lists 25 distinct commits before PR #401, and 11 PRs merged during the Chicago reporting day. The live dated API reports commitCount 32 because build-api counts every backticked seven-character SHA occurrence when frontmatter lacks commitCount; repeated/candidate references inflate this derived field.
findings.correction: Preserve 25 as the sourced activity count; set an explicit count for the projection or otherwise prevent the heuristic 32 from being presented as distinct commits.
